messages.subject: Dataframe Organization for Facetting
parts:
I'd like to ask for advice how to organize a data frame to benefit
from facetting in ggplot2. I have data from a user survey in an SQL
database which I'd like to import into a dataframe and analyze using
ggplot2. One record of survey data consists of (say) 10 numbers, each
an answer to a question q1 .. q10.

At the database level q1 up to q10 are columns such that each row
(record) consists of an ID and 10 columns. What would be the best way
to organize the dataframe for R? "The R Book" suggests to have all
responses in one column and to label each one using a factor.
Unfortunately, I find this difficult to realize during an import. What
do you recommend?

-- Christian

messages.author: 3c30c52b0f668f28
messages.subject: Re: Dataframe Organization for Facetting
parts:
It is difficult during an import, but it is very easy to do after import with reshape package and melt function. For example :
df <- data.frame(id = 1:10, q1 = rnorm(10), q2 = rnorm(10), q3 = rnorm(10))
df
melt(df)

David
